Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations. Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.

  CITY OF AZUSA
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE AZUSA UTILITY BOARD
  & SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 23, 2024– 6:30 P.M.

Chairperson:  Edward J. Alvarez
Vice Chairperson:  Jesse Avila, Jr.
Board Member:  Robert Gonzales
Board Member:  Andrew N. Mendez
Board Member:  Dennis Beckwith
Secretary:  Jeffrey Lawrence Cornejo, Jr.

The Utility Board of the City of Azusa met in regular session, at the above date and time, in the Azusa Light &
Water First Floor Conference Room located at 729 N. Azusa Avenue, Azusa, California.

Chairperson Alvarez called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by Secretary Cornejo.

PRESENT: BOARD MEMBERS:  AVILA Jr., ALVAREZ, GONZALES, MENDEZ, BECKWITH
ABSENT: BOARD MEMBERS:

The pledge to the flag was led by Chair Alvarez.

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: Secretary Cornejo
City Attorney:  Marco Martinez
Staff Members:  City Manager Sergio Gonzalez, General Manager Tikan Singh, Assistant General Manager
Richard Torres, Assistant General Manager Water Operations Melissa Barbosa, Assistant General Manager Hien
Vuong, Assistant General Manager Alicia Holmes, Environmental Programs Manager Paul Reid, Senior
Management Analyst Yesenia Paez, Chief of Police Rocky Wenrick, Chief Deputy City Clerk Adrian Garcia.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

None.

CLOSED SESSION

None.

Chairperson Alvarez called the Regular to order at 6:30 P.M.
 GENERAL MANAGER COMMENTS

General Manager Singh reported that the annual Azusa Shred-A-Thon event was successful. There are two events
held per year in April and September. On September 21, 2024 there were 195 cars dropoffs and 7,340 pounds of
paper shredded. The next Compost-Mulch Giveaway event is scheduled for September 28, 2024 at the Memorial
Park Parking Lot.

General Manager Singh answered Board Member questions.

UTILITY BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS

Board Member Gonzales thanked staff for a successful shred event. The Azusa High School football team will be
joining the group to help residents obtain compost and mulch on September 28, 2024.

  1. Award of Contract for South Reservoir Capital Improvement Project WF-221.
  Recommendation: 1) Approve the Award of Contract to Pacific Hydrotech Corporation for the
  construction of South Reservoir Capital Improvement Project No. WF-221, in the amount not-to-exceed
  $10,704,328.80; and 2) Authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order for a not to exceed price of
  $10,704,328.80 in accordance with Azusa Municipal Code Sec 2-518 – Contracts; and 3) Authorize the
  Mayor to execute the Contract, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.

MOTION by Board Member Beckwith, seconded by Board Member Avila Jr., to approve the Award of Contract
to Pacific Hydrotech Corporation for the construction of South Reservoir Capital Improvement Project No. WF-

price of $10,704,328.80 in accordance with Azusa Municipal Code Sec 2-518 – Contracts; and Authorize the Mayor
to execute the Contract, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.

STAFF REPORTS/COMMUNICATIONS

None.

VERBAL COMMUNICATIONS

  1. Power Supply Update

  Assistant General Manager Torres reported Summer 2024 highlights. In July and August, Downtown Los
  Angeles (DTLA) averaged 85/87 degrees, 2-3 degrees higher than average. Azusa’s all-time high was 71.2
  MW set in September 2022. At that time, DTLA had an average of 99 degrees and Riverside averaged 107
  degrees. On Thursday, September 5, 2024, Azusa’s peak was 73.75 MW. On September 6, 2024, Azusa
  reached a new all-time high of 76.49 MW. DTLA reached 112 degrees and Riverside reached 115 degrees.
  The 2024 renewable state target is 44%; Azusa Year to Date is 45%. Azusa is looking at warmer than
  average temperatures through December.

  Assistant General Manager Torres responded to Board Member questions.

  2. Water Supply Update

PAGE 3 – 9/2/24
   Assistant General Manager Water Operations Barbosa reported that as of September 13, 2024, the key well
  is at approximately 242.8 feet. State reservoirs are at approximately 70% capacity. As Upper District is
  delivering water, San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District is delivering water to the basin. The
  Membrane Replacement Project was estimated to be $600,000. The project came under budget at $475,000.
  Staff changed out 400 modulars n three units. Delivery came in August and took about a month for staff to
  install. The modulars will last around five to eight years. SWP allocation is at 40% and SGVMWD balance
  is 8,373 AF/11,520 AF.

  Assistant General Manager Water Operations Barbosa responded to Board Member questions.
